newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Russia seen importing 4 mln tonnes grain in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia seen importing 4 mln tonnes grain in 1997.

text.p: Russia's agriculture minister Viktor Khlystun said on Monday Russia would import about four million tonnes of mainly corn and soy in 1997 but export about the same amount for a zero grain trade balance.
"In 1997 we plan to buy not more than four million tonnes," Khlystun told Reuters during a during a visit to Sweden.
"This includes mainly soy and corn but also some grain, mostly for Russia's Far East region."
Khlystun said most of this would be bought from the U.S., Canada and Australia. "It is from the countries that specialise in corn and soy," he said.
He said the transportation infrastructure made importing grain to Russia's Far East region from western Russia more expensive than importing it.
"To transport grain from Europe...I mean Russian Europe, makes it much more expensive than bringing it from over the ocean," he said.
Khlystun said Russia planned to export the same amount of grain to countries such as Georgia, Azerbaijan, Armenia and Moldova next year.
"But we will sell about the same amount of grain to other countries that we plan to buy -- to Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Moldova.
"The balance between imports and exports will be about zero for grain," he said.
Russia would import from wherever it received the best offer.
"From wherever we are offered the best terms -- maybe Canada, the U.S., Australia or Argentina.
"But the largest part of the import will consist of corn and soy," he stressed.
Preliminary data from Russia's State Statistic Committee showed this year's gross grain harvest was 74.6 million tonnes, just eight percent up on 1995's disastrous 30-year low.
